objective.text: Design an outbox to close the commit-versus-publish failure window without claiming exactly-once delivery.

difficulty.rationale: Resolve the atomicity gap between local commit and remote publication while accounting for relay retries.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: An order commits, then the process crashes before publishing OrderAccepted to a broker. The event must remain recoverable without a distributed transaction. Which design also accounts for a relay crash after publishing?

options.text: Use only an in-memory afterCommit callback and consider publication guaranteed once commit succeeds.
options.rationale: A process can die after commit but before the callback publishes, leaving no durable publication work item.
options.misconception: A process can die after commit but before the callback publishes, leaving no durable publication work item.

options.text: Commit an outbox row and mark it sent before publishing, so consumers never receive duplicates.
options.rationale: A crash after marking sent but before publishing loses the event; avoiding duplicates this way sacrifices recoverability.
options.misconception: A crash after marking sent but before publishing loses the event; avoiding duplicates this way sacrifices recoverability.

options.text: Publish before the database commit and assume a later rollback retracts the broker message.
options.rationale: A local rollback cannot retract an already published remote message.
options.misconception: A local rollback cannot retract an already published remote message.

options.text: Commit the order and an outbox row together; retry relay delivery using a stable event ID and idempotent consumers.
options.rationale: The durable outbox survives a post-commit process crash. A relay may publish twice after an ambiguous acknowledgment, so consumers must tolerate duplicates.

validation.reason: A local transaction can commit the domain row and outbox row atomically. Relay failure-window and consumer-idempotency claims use the cited original outbox pattern; no broker execution or exactly-once guarantee is claimed.
